GeoSpaX recipes: read, validate, run and write

geo-recipe.Rd

A recipe is a GeoSpaX workflow saved as YAML (format version 1): inputs, a list of steps that use named tools, and outputs. These functions let tidymapr and the GeoSpaX desktop GIS share recipes:

  • geo_recipe_read() reads a recipe file (or YAML text);

  • geo_recipe_validate() checks it as GeoSpaX does, reporting every problem at once before anything runs: the recipe id, unknown steps, ${...} references to steps or inputs that do not exist, missing dependencies and circular ones. Steps that exist in GeoSpaX but not in tidymapr are listed as such;

  • geo_recipe_run() runs a recipe in R with tidymapr's tools;

  • geo_recipe(), recipe_input() and recipe_step() build a recipe in R, and geo_recipe_write() saves it for GeoSpaX.

Steps that tidymapr runs:

GeoSpaX steptidymapr
io.opengeo_read()
interpolate.idwgeo_interpolate() (method = "idw")
interpolate.autokriging against IDW by leave-one-out error, with a standard-error map
aggregate.hexbinpoints counted (or summed or averaged) in auto-sized hexagons
stats.hotspotsgeo_hotspot() (Getis-Ord Gi*), on hexagon counts when no field is given
automap.stylethe geo_automap() rules
export.mapa geo_automap() page saved as PNG, SVG or PDF
export.datageo_write()
export.reportan HTML report with the maps, every automatic decision and the run log
terrain.derivegeo_raster_terrain()
rs.indexgeo_spectral_index() on a raster you give

Other GeoSpaX steps (device import, LiDAR, 3D scenes, online data fetches, GRASS/SAGA, AI models) are reported by geo_recipe_validate() and stop geo_recipe_run() with a clear message: run those recipes in GeoSpaX.

Expressions follow GeoSpaX: ${inputs.x}, ${step.key}, ${step.list.0}, ${run.date}, ${recipe}, and fallbacks such as ${inputs.title ?? Field map}. A string that is exactly one ${...} keeps the referenced value's type.

Usage

geo_recipe_read(path)

geo_recipe(id, title = id, description = NULL)

recipe_input(recipe, name, type = "layer", default = NULL, description = NULL)

recipe_step(recipe, id, use, ..., needs = NULL, when = NULL)

geo_recipe_write(x, path)

geo_recipe_validate(x)

geo_recipe_run(
  x,
  inputs = list(),
  dir = tempfile("recipe-run-"),
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Path to a recipe file (.yaml, .yml or .json), or YAML text.

id, title, description

Recipe id (a-z 0-9 - _), title and description.

recipe

A recipe to add to.

name, type, default

Input name, type ("layer", "field", "text", ...) and default value.

use

GeoSpaX step name, for example "export.map".

...

Step parameters (the step's with:).

needs, when

Extra ordering (step ids) and a run condition.

x

A recipe from geo_recipe_read() or geo_recipe().

inputs

Named list of recipe inputs. Layers can be file paths or sf / SpatRaster objects.

dir

Folder for the run's outputs (maps, data, report).

quiet

Suppress progress messages?

Value

geo_recipe_read() and geo_recipe(): a tmr_recipe. geo_recipe_validate(): a tibble of problems (severity, step, problem), empty when the recipe is valid. geo_recipe_run(): a list with each step's outputs, the run log and the output folder. geo_recipe_write(): path, invisibly.

See also

geo_automap(), geo_interpolate(), geo_hotspot()

Examples

# A recipe shipped with GeoSpaX: point samples to an interpolated surface
rec <- geo_recipe_read(system.file("recipes/interpolate-samples.yaml", package = "tidymapr"))
rec
#> GeoSpaX recipe "interpolate-samples" (v2): Field samples → interpolated surface
#> (kriging or IDW, automatically)
#> Inputs: layer and field
#> Steps: samples (io.open), surface (interpolate.auto), style_samples
#> (automap.style), map (export.map), uncertainty (export.map), and report
#> (export.report)
#> Outputs: surface, map, uncertainty, and report
geo_recipe_validate(rec)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 3
#> # ℹ 3 variables: severity <chr>, step <chr>, problem <chr>

# Run it on the Meuse river soil samples (zinc, mg/kg; shipped with terra)
meuse <- terra::unwrap(readRDS(system.file("ex/meuse.rds", package = "terra")))
samples <- sf::st_as_sf(meuse, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 28992)
out <- geo_recipe_run(rec, inputs = list(layer = samples, field = "zinc"))
#> samples (io.open)
#> surface (interpolate.auto)
#> style_samples (automap.style)
#> map (export.map)
#> uncertainty (export.map)
#> report (export.report)
out$surface$method_label
#> [1] "ordinary kriging, exponential variogram"
list.files(out$dir)
#> [1] "map.png"         "report.html"     "uncertainty.png"

# Build a recipe in R and save it for GeoSpaX
r <- geo_recipe("zinc-hotspots", "Zinc hot spots") |>
  recipe_input("layer", "layer", description = "soil samples") |>
  recipe_step("samples", "io.open", layer = "${inputs.layer}") |>
  recipe_step("hot", "stats.hotspots", layer = "${samples.layer}", field = "zinc") |>
  recipe_step("map", "export.map", layers = list("${hot.layer}"), scale_bar = "checker")
geo_recipe_validate(r)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 3
#> # ℹ 3 variables: severity <chr>, step <chr>, problem <chr>
geo_recipe_write(r, tempfile(fileext = ".yaml"))
